userStories.title: Replace the remaining legacy decisions with keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace the remaining admin-claim shortcuts with their declared capabilities and enforce the workspace stream read key.

**Motivation** — Listing projects, the home dashboard, pickup on another agent's behalf, the last-admin override and assignee eligibility each read `role === 'ADMIN'` from a principal or a user row.

**Approach** — The remaining decisions (US-002)

| Site | Baseline (locate only) | Target |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `ProjectsService.findAllForPrincipal` | `principal.actorType === 'user' && principal.role === 'ADMIN'` → `findAll()` | `await this.access.readsEveryProject(principal)` → `findAll()`, checked first. The agent branch (roster, or every project when scoping is off) and the user branch (`findAllForUser`) are unchanged. |
| `HomeController.get` | `globalAdmin: principal.role === 'ADMIN'` | `globalAdmin: (await this.permissions.can(principal, 'project.read')).allowed`. The constructor gains `PermissionService` as its second parameter. The agent refusal is unchanged. |
| `AgentsService.suggestTicket` | `isGlobalAdmin = principal.actorType === 'user' && principal.role === 'ADMIN'` | A caller that is not the owning agent passes when `(await this.permissions.can(principal, 'agent.update')).allowed`; otherwise 403 `agents`, as today. `can` is not asked for the owning agent. |
| `TicketsService.assign`, user assignee | skip the check when `user.role === 'ADMIN'`, else 403 `tickets` when `findProjectMemberRole` is null | 403 `tickets` unless `(await this.permissions.effectiveKeys({ type: 'USER', id: user.id }, { projectId: project.id })).has('project.read')`. The not-found, disabled and agent-assignee checks are unchanged. |
| `ProjectMembersService.assertKeepsAnAdmin` | `isGlobalAdmin(principal)` (`principal.role === 'ADMIN'`) skips the last-admin count | Only when the change loses an active admin, `(await this.permissions.can(principal, 'role.binding.global')).allowed` skips the count; a change that loses no admin asks nothing. The module-level `isGlobalAdmin` is deleted. |
| `WorkspaceThreadEventsController` | `@UseGuards(WorkspaceThreadEventsGuard)`; `@Requires('thread.workspace.read', { enforcedBy: 'service' })` | `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard, WorkspaceThreadEventsGuard)` at the class level, in that order; `@Requires('thread.workspace.read')` (guard). `WorkspaceThreadEventsGuard`'s ownership fence (404 `threads.notFound`), JWT and stream-slot checks are unchanged. |

- The workspace REST reads already declare `thread.workspace.read` with `RequiresGuard`. `RequiresGuard` passes a caller holding only `thread.workspace.read.own` (reason `not-owner`), so a Member's own stream behaves as today.
- `agent.update` and `role.binding.global` are `granted` only for `owner` and `admin` in the role matrix, globally and in `p1`.

**Scope** — In: the six sites above, their existing service/route/declaration test harnesses, and the custom GLOBAL project.read project-list integration. Out: the central access gate (US-001), domain writer (US-003), role-bearing request/context removal (US-004), and deleting the now-unused repository method and helper mechanisms (US-005). Do not change home content beyond the globalAdmin source or make home/me-events serve agents. Do not migrate ProjectAssigneesService.search, recipient selection, legacy fixture sources or the compatibility union.

**Interface** — Preserve the existing signatures of `ProjectsService.findAllForPrincipal`, `HomeController.get`, `AgentsService.suggestTicket`, `TicketsService.assign`, `ProjectMembersService.assertKeepsAnAdmin` and `WorkspaceThreadEventsController.events`. The exact key calls, constructor addition and decorator forms are specified verbatim in the table. Use US-001's `readsEveryProject(principal: KodaPrincipal): Promise<boolean>` rather than recreating its logic.

**Implementation and verification notes** — PermissionService is required and globally available. Check caller agent.update before looking up target-agent keys; owning-agent pickup never asks can but still checks the target's agent.pickup. Preserve disabled/not-found user checks, agent roster locking, transactional assignment and all event envelopes. A user lacking project.read must not be assigned. The last-admin override asks nothing for a change that loses no active admin. Guard ordering must refuse the workspace read key before ownership, JWT capacity acquisition or SSE opening; baseline-agent-only own threads now get 403 permissions. Keep .own pass-through and the ownership 404 fence for otherwise admitted callers. Update allow-all permission doubles in unauthorized pickup/last-admin cases to refuse the exact key, add effectiveKeys to assignment doubles including the outbox-envelope integration harness, and switch only the workspace-stream row of remaining-route-declarations.spec.ts to guard mode. Run the project-list integration with system roles seeded and a MEMBER user holding both member and a custom GLOBAL ['project.read'] binding but no project source.

userStories.title: Authorize domain event writers through project access
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace KodaDomainWriter's legacy actor-role allow-list with the actor's effective project.read key before each event transaction.

**Motivation** — It omits `VERIFIER`, so the `TICKET_SUGGESTED` event of a pickup by an agent whose only legacy role is `VERIFIER` is refused after the pickup itself was allowed.

**Approach** — The domain writer (US-003)

`apps/api/src/koda-domain-writer/koda-domain-writer.service.ts`:
- `KodaDomainWriter`'s fourth constructor parameter changes from `AgentAuthProvider` to `PermissionService`. The other parameters keep their positions.
- `assertActorHasEventRole` is replaced:

```ts
/** The actor must have access to the project the event belongs to: the same key project routes are gated on. */
private async assertActorInProject(actor: PrincipalRef, projectId: string): Promise<void> {
  const keys = await this.permissions.effectiveKeys(actor, { projectId });
  if (!keys.has(PROJECT_ACCESS_KEY)) throw new ForbiddenAppException({}, 'koda-domain-writer');
}
```

- The actor of each write:
  - `writeTicketEvent`: `{ type: data.actorType === 'agent' ? 'AGENT' : 'USER', id: data.actorId }`;
  - `writeAgentAction` and `writeDecisionEvent`: `{ type: 'AGENT', id: data.agentId }`.
- Each write checks the actor after `assertProjectExists` and before its transaction, as the role check did.
- `PrismaKodaDomainWriterRepository.findUserProjectRoles` is deleted.
- `KodaDomainWriterModule` drops its `AuthModule` import, which served only `AgentAuthProvider`.
- The legacy-membership compat doc already lists the domain writer as a reader of who may act in a project. The key is the same decision, so drop-legacy has nothing left to move here.

**Scope** — In: the three actor-scoped event writes, constructor/provider replacement, deletion of the obsolete repository reader and reader-only tests, plus viewer/no-source and VERIFIER pickup integration regressions. Out: the access service implementation (US-001), caller pickup shortcut and assignee checks (US-002), request/context cleanup (US-004), and remaining CASL/tool/helper deletions (US-005). Do not remove AgentAuthProvider.loadAgentRoles elsewhere, migrate legacy fixture sources or change approval/audit policies. Do not add actor authorization to indexDocument/importGraphify beyond this story's specified three event writes.

**Interface** — `private async assertActorInProject(actor: PrincipalRef, projectId: string): Promise<void>` is declared verbatim above; the fourth KodaDomainWriter constructor parameter is PermissionService and all other positions remain unchanged. Use `PrincipalRef` from permissions/permissions.types.ts and `PROJECT_ACCESS_KEY` exported by US-001.

**Implementation and verification notes** — Refuse without the key using 403 koda-domain-writer, regardless of supplied payload role, legacy actor role list or ADMIN claim. Refusal must create no event and no outbox row; missing project must fail before effectiveKeys. Preserve validation, canonical IDs, provenance, event envelopes and atomic commit/rollback semantics. The viewer-only binding now grants event writing; an agent with no legacy roles no longer bypasses project access. Replace AgentAuthProvider doubles in the writer service/provenance/event operations/writer integration suites with PermissionService.effectiveKeys doubles, remove find-user-project-roles.spec.ts and its obsolete contract describe, and add effectiveKeys to producer-atomicity's existing permission double. In membership-ticket-consumers, change only the viewer refusal expectation to a stored event and introduce the no-source refusal. Seed roles before DB cases and invalidate cached keys after direct fixture writes. The pickup integration must boot the real app and authenticate the rostered VERIFIER-only agent with its own API key.

userStories.title: Retire CASL and the dead legacy permission mechanisms
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Delete the custom CASL factory and unused legacy permission mechanisms after their live decision paths have migrated.

**Motivation** — The CASL factory, the project-permission decorators and their guard steps, the tool `permission` field, `assertTransitionPermission`, `canOverrideClose` and several helpers have no live caller.

**Approach** — Dead mechanisms (US-005)

| Symbol | File(s) under `apps/api/src/` | Target |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `KodaCaslAbilityFactory`, its spec | `auth/casl/koda-casl-ability.factory.ts`, `auth/casl/koda-casl-ability.factory.spec.ts` | deleted |
| `KodaAction`, `KodaSubject` | `auth/casl/koda-action.enum.ts` | deleted |
| CASL registration | `auth/auth.module.ts` | `caslAbilityFactory` option, provider and export removed; nestjs-auth then provides its default `JwtCaslAbilityFactory` |
| CASL provider | `projects/project-access.module.ts` | `KodaCaslAbilityFactory` provider, export and comment removed |
| `UserPrincipal.projectRole` | `auth/principal/koda-principal.types.ts`, `auth/jwt-auth.provider.ts` | field removed; `JwtAuthProvider.getPrincipal` sets no `projectRole` property, and its SECURITY comments are reduced to the claim allow-list |
| `TicketTransitionsService.assertTransitionPermission`, `caslAbilityFactory` parameter | `tickets/state-machine/ticket-transitions.service.ts` | removed (the last constructor parameter, `@Optional()`) |
| `updateTicketTool` `transitions` dependency | `fleet/assistant/tools/update-ticket-tool.ts`, `fleet/assistant/tools/ticket-write-tools.ts` | `updateTicketTool({ tickets })`; `TicketWriteTools` drops its `TicketTransitionsService` parameter |
| `ToolPermission`, `AssistantTool.permission` | `fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.types.ts` and the 14 tool files under `fleet/assistant/tools/` that set `permission:` | removed; `ToolForbiddenError`'s doc names a key, not an ability |
| `canOverrideClose` | `tickets/state-machine/allowed-actions.ts` | deleted |
| `ProjectAccessService.assertProjectAdmin`, `canManageMembers` | `projects/project-access.service.ts` | deleted |
| `ProjectsService.assertProjectMembership`, `assertProjectAdmin`, `findMembershipRole` | `projects/projects.service.ts` | deleted (no caller) |
| `ITicketRepository.findProjectMemberRole` | `tickets/domain/ticket.domain.ts`, `tickets/prisma-tickets.repository.ts` | deleted (no caller after US-002) |
| `FleetActivityService.memberProjectIds`, `findMemberProjectIds` | `fleet/activity/fleet-activity.service.ts`, `fleet/activity/domain/fleet-activity.domain.ts`, `fleet/activity/prisma-fleet-activity.repository.ts` | deleted |
| `ApprovalsService`'s `activity` parameter | `fleet/approvals/approvals.service.ts` | removed (the seventh parameter, after `live`; `txManager` and the later ones move up one place) |
| `ApprovalCaller.globalAdmin` | `fleet/approvals/approvals.service.ts`, `fleet/approvals/fleet-approvals.controller.ts`, `fleet/approvals/project-fleet-approvals.controller.ts` | field removed; both controllers pass `{ id, principal }` |
| IN_PROGRESS → VERIFIED rule | `tickets/state-machine/ticket-transitions.ts` | removed from `TRANSITION_RULES` with its comment; the comments in `transition-keys.ts` and `ticket-transitions.service.ts` that name it are reworded |
| `skills.principal`, `skills.projectPrincipal` | `i18n/en/skills.json`, `i18n/zh/skills.json` | removed (no code reads them since enforce-integrations) |
| comments naming the factory | `common/enums.ts`, `ticket-links/ticket-links.module.ts` | reworded |

- `PATCH` with `status: 'VERIFIED'` on an `IN_PROGRESS` ticket still answers 400 `tickets`: `validateTransition` throws the same `ValidationAppException` for a missing rule as for a missing comment.
- The CASL-only test files are deleted (see Modifies). They test only the factory's grants.

**Scope** — In: every deletion/reduction in the table, obsolete-only test file/describe removal, positional constructor corrections, tool key assertion preservation, default Nathapp factory integration and the rejected-transition regression. Out: the live access/key migrations (US-001/002/003), guard/decorator/context cleanup (US-004), fixture conversion, legacy schema/union/fallback removal, findMembershipRole on the access service/repository, AgentPrincipal.agentRoles, AgentAuthProvider.loadAgentRoles, scoping flag/update-roles route, JWT role claim changes, notification-recipient selection and web viewerRole replacement. Do not delete the placeholder context-controller.integration.spec.ts or change approval policies, the audit log or ActionContext.

**Interface** — `updateTicketTool({ tickets })` replaces the old dependency object. The project route is already `{ kind: 'project'; projectId: string }` from US-004; approval controllers now pass `{ id, principal }` without globalAdmin. Retain UserPrincipal.role but omit any own projectRole field from JwtAuthProvider results. Deleting the optional last TicketTransitionsService parameter must not alter earlier constructor positions; deleting ApprovalsService parameter seven moves all later positional arguments up one place.

**Implementation and verification notes** — Delete the custom factory implementation, action/subject enum file, colocated factory spec, test/unit/auth/koda-casl-ability.factory.spec.ts, test/integration/ast-index/ast-index-casl-permissions.integration.spec.ts, test/integration/code-intel/codeintel-casl-permissions.integration.spec.ts and test/integration/rag/import-graphify-permission.integration.spec.ts. Remove obsolete factory imports/provider entries from webhook routes, transitions service, project guard routes, producer atomicity and ticket tenancy harnesses, preserving every non-CASL outcome. Remove only the describes for assertTransitionPermission, canOverrideClose, findMemberProjectIds, the access admin helpers and ProjectsService wrappers. The access service's own assertProjectMembership and findMembershipRole remain live. Drop update-ticket-tool's unused transitions harness/assertion and replace all tool.permission assertions in the listed tool specs and assistant.module.spec.ts with each tool's already-declared key (add a key assertion when absent). Preserve all live tool key checks and behavior. JWT security tests must check absence of an own projectRole property rather than just an undefined value; role, authorities, extra and revocation behavior remain. The two former GENERAL-comment transition acceptance cases now reject, and all other transition outcomes stay.
Verify deletion completeness by review and bun run --cwd apps/api type-check, bun run --cwd apps/api lint and bun run --cwd apps/api test, with deleted files actually absent. Runtime integration uses bootHttpApp to observe the default JwtCaslAbilityFactory and 400 tickets without status mutation. The catalog contract and committed role matrix remain regression anchors, not snapshots to update for cleanup. Real DB cases seed system roles after resetDb or boot the app; direct membership/binding fixture mutations require MembershipService.invalidatePermissions. Only existing e2e cases broken by the correct implementation are edited; do not expand this deletion story into new endpoint-e2e coverage.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] validateTransition(TicketStatus.IN_PROGRESS, TicketStatus.VERIFIED, CommentType.GENERAL) throws ValidationAppException.
[unit] The keys of TRANSITION_RULES[TicketStatus.IN_PROGRESS] equal exactly [TicketStatus.VERIFY_FIX].

[unit] JwtAuthProvider.getPrincipal for a JWT payload { sub, email, role: 'MEMBER', tokenVersion: 0, projectRole: 'ADMIN' } returns a principal equal to the one it returns for the same payload without projectRole.
[integration] In the app booted by bootHttpApp, app.get(CaslAbilityFactory, { strict: false }) from @nathapp/nestjs-auth is an instance of JwtCaslAbilityFactory.

[integration] In the booted app, PATCH /projects/p1/tickets/<ref> with { status: 'VERIFIED' } on an IN_PROGRESS ticket by a global admin answers 400 with error code tickets, and the ticket stays IN_PROGRESS.

analysis:
EXPLORATION AND ARCHITECTURE
Codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this session; findings were verified by direct file reads and targeted text searches. This is an existing API refactor, not greenfield work. All implementation is scoped to apps/api. The supplied auto-detected Express/Next.js labels are not the architecture authority: .nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:13 and :27 identify the system-of-record API as NestJS 12 + Fastify, Prisma 7, Vitest and oxlint; the web is a separate Nuxt client per repository guidance. apps/api/package.json:10-24 confirms Vitest unit/scoped/DB scripts, oxlint and tsc --noEmit; :46-56 and :69-71 show the installed Nathapp and Nest dependencies. Do not introduce a framework or dependency migration. Read nathapp-nestjs-patterns before implementation; no skill file matching that name is exposed inside this checkout. .nax/rules/api-auth.md:10-28 and .nax/rules/api-core.md:17-22 already describe the intended key-based architecture; do not restore CASL or role-based authorization to match old tests.

REFINE AUDIT AND FIXTURE DEFINITIONS
All 54 numbered spec criteria are retained in their original stories and order: US-001 criteria 1-13, US-002 criteria 1-15, US-003 criteria 1-11, US-004 criteria 1-10 and US-005 criteria 1-5. Their concrete identifiers, principal/object identity requirements, fixture conditions and qualifying clauses remain intact. The additional US-003 criterion explicitly covers the failure table's no-event/no-outbox outcome for the three event-write methods only; it does not extend authorization to indexDocument or importGraphify. All six failure-table rows map to observable criteria: US-001 8 (same database error), US-001 11 (projects refusal before RequiresGuard), US-002 7/8 (agents refusal before target keys), US-002 10 (tickets refusal without assignment), US-003 3/6/7/10/12 (writer refusal with no writes), US-002 14 (permissions refusal before ownership/stream slot). Every story already has a negative path and regression anchors; no invented failure criterion is needed. The eleven feature exclusions are preserved verbatim in outOfScope. All five contextFiles lists match the spec's five primary recommendations; none is newly created or removed by an upstream story. Binding dependencies remain unchanged. Security-critical three-session-tdd remains mandatory for all stories; US-001 is medium rather than complex because its production algorithm is localized to one existing service with established collaborators.
Fixture wording is binding: a user whose only source in p1 is a <role> binding has that RoleBinding in p1, no ProjectMember row, and User.role = 'MEMBER'. A global admin is a user with a global admin binding. A custom PROJECT role with [...] is a Role row with scope PROJECT, system: false and exactly those permission entries. Unit permission answers come from PermissionService doubles; DB-backed cases seed system roles after resetDb or boot the app. Use the real project id in permission contexts, not the slug. Distinguish omitted context in direct global can calls from RequiresGuard's existing empty-context call; do not change RequiresGuard to force two-argument calls. Re-reading ProjectMembersService.remove confirms its first argument is a slug (apps/api/src/projects/members/project-members.service.ts:96-103): the AC's 'proj' is resolved to projectId through access.findProjectIdBySlug before the key/count checks. Re-reading AssistantToolExecutor confirms that null display role is admitted and only undefined denotes refused membership (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.executor.ts:130-135, :255-269 and :283-289); preserve that distinction while removing role decoration.

GOAL AND DEPENDENCY ORDER
This is one capability, the eighth P1 feature, following contract-tests (PR #317). Preserve exactly US-001 through US-005: US-001 establishes project.read access and the global query; US-002, US-003 and US-004 each depend on US-001; US-005 depends on all three. Cleanup order is contract-tests, retire-checks, fixtures-to-bindings, drop-legacy; permissions-p1-web runs in parallel and must land before drop-legacy, not before this feature. The design document predates the split and is not to be edited. No schema/data migration, approval-policy change, audit change, ActionContext work or fixture conversion is part of this run.

SHARED AUTHORIZATION CONTRACT
apps/api/src/permissions/permissions.module.ts:21-34 explains the global module; :49-54 provides and exports PermissionService, MembershipService and RoleAdminService. Consumers inject PermissionService as required, without @Optional(). apps/api/src/permissions/permission.service.ts:32-40 documents the legacy-row/binding/baseline union and caching; :53-87 implements can and effectiveKeys, and :121-149 preserves legacy compatibility. Keep that union, fallback and isLegacyAdmin untouched. A refused catalog key normally uses new ForbiddenAppException({}, 'permissions'), while the project access gate retains 403 projects. Existing specialized refusals remain agents, tickets and koda-domain-writer as explicitly specified. PermissionService errors propagate, never become invented 403s. effectiveKeys takes PrincipalRef plus { projectId } (or 'global'); can takes the principal and optionally a context. Global capability checks must omit projectId rather than infer them from a project grant.
The committed matrix confirms project.read global grants at apps/api/src/permissions/__snapshots__/role-matrix.json:132 and :355, baseline refusals at :578 and :801, and project grants at :1024, :1247, :1470, :1693, :1916, :2139 and :2362. agent.update and role.binding.global are granted only to owner/admin, e.g. :7, :217, :230, :440 versus :453 and :663. Do not update the matrix or catalog to make cleanup pass.
Behavior remains the same for seeded roles except the explicit rulings: a viewer or legacy VERIFIER-only actor with project access may write domain events; a no-role agent now needs project.read for those writes; principal role claims no longer override bindings; a legacy ProjectMember role such as MEMBER is admitted through its viewer virtual binding; globally bound owner/admin agents or custom GLOBAL project.read agents gain all-project access/listing; workspace streams require thread.workspace.read or its .own capability before the ownership fence; viewerRole stays unchanged for previously admitted users and becomes ADMIN for any global project.read holder, otherwise the stored legacy/display role or null. Keep UserPrincipal.role, JWT role claims, AgentPrincipal.agentRoles, findMembershipRole, AGENT_PROJECT_SCOPING and disabled/not-found/agent-roster invariants.

US-001 FINDINGS AND IMPACT
apps/api/src/projects/project-access.service.ts:10-13 currently accepts (projectRepo, optional authConfig); :45-64 uses the user's ADMIN claim and a stored-role allow-list, or agent roster reads, to admit. Replace this one decision with the specified can(project.read, { projectId }); runners and scoping-off agents bypass the ask. Add required PermissionService in position two, shift auth config to position three, export PROJECT_ACCESS_KEY, and add readsEveryProject with a runner false shortcut. Display role still comes from the repository unless global project.read is held. assertProjectMembership at :66-68 remains a delegation, so guard, comments, members, assistant, memory and live/thread-stream callers adopt the key gate without per-caller rewrites. findMembershipRole at :75-77 must stay. The two dead admin helpers at :83-97 remain until US-005 to keep the dependency sequence coherent. The central gate has a broad security blast radius: an apparently harmless constructor or mock change can accidentally admit all principals or invent a fallback.
Tests to adapt in US-001: src/projects/project-access.service.spec.ts; test/unit/projects/agent-project-access.spec.ts; src/projects/projects.service.spec.ts; src/projects/project-membership.guard.spec.ts; src/projects/project-membership.guard.routes.spec.ts; src/retrieval/retrieval-membership.routes.spec.ts; src/rag/kb-documents-membership.routes.spec.ts; test/unit/projects/projects-find-all-for-principal.spec.ts (all paths under apps/api). Supply PermissionService doubles in the new constructor slot. Model refusals with project.read in refusedKeys rather than null membership/false roster answers. Replace admission-related roster/repository call assertions with can(principal, 'project.read', { projectId }) assertions; retain actual display-role reads. Agent scoping-off and runner cases never ask can. Existing wrapper/admin-helper test outcomes remain until US-005. apps/api/test/integration/permissions/membership-project-access.integration.spec.ts:1-18 is the real-HTTP compatibility suite; :76-77 creates bindings through MembershipService and :103-108 boots after resetDb. Extend existing integration fixtures for custom no-project.read roles and viewerRole regressions, without converting legacy fixture sources.

US-002 FINDINGS AND IMPACT
apps/api/src/projects/projects.service.ts:80-89 checks user ADMIN before the agent branch: replace that first condition with await access.readsEveryProject(principal) for both users and agents; keep remaining roster/scoping/user queries. apps/api/src/home/home.controller.ts:23 and :31-33 require a second constructor dependency and await can(user, 'project.read') for globalAdmin; agents remain refused and home.read remains implicit. apps/api/src/agents/agents.service.ts:386-396 currently authorizes another agent's pickup by the user ADMIN claim. Replace only that caller shortcut with agent.update; owning agents short-circuit and never call can. Preserve the target effectiveKeys(agent.pickup) check at :408-414 and perform no target lookup/key read when caller authority fails. The suggested-ticket event at :438-443 is the integration seam into US-003. apps/api/src/tickets/tickets.service.ts:412-468 performs assignment inside txManager.run, with disabled-user check before role/member eligibility at :446-460. Replace just that eligibility with the assignee's effectiveKeys({ type: 'USER', id }, { projectId }).has('project.read'); do not change the agent-roster lock, disabled-user conflict, not-found outcomes, event envelopes or transactional assignment. apps/api/src/projects/members/project-members.service.ts:119-131 computes losesAdmin, then applies the legacy override: only ask role.binding.global when losesAdmin, otherwise do not ask it or count admins. Remove the module-level isGlobalAdmin helper.
apps/api/src/fleet/threads/workspace-thread-events.controller.ts:40-50 currently checks ownership, JWT and capacity in its guard; :59 and :69 register only that guard and service-mode Requires. Put RequiresGuard before WorkspaceThreadEventsGuard at class level and switch the declaration to guard mode; denied callers must not reach requireOwnedThread or consume a slot. apps/api/src/permissions/requires.guard.ts:35-59 already accepts reason not-owner to let X.own holders reach the service fence; no new guard algorithm is needed. apps/api/src/permissions/remaining-route-declarations.spec.ts:21 pins this stream to service mode and must change to guard, with other rows preserved.
Tests to adapt in US-002: test/unit/projects/projects-find-all-for-principal.spec.ts (global query decided by double, including ADMIN-claim refusal); src/home/home.controller.spec.ts (second constructor argument); src/agents/agents-pickup.routes.spec.ts (refuse agent.update for unauthorized callers instead of using an allow-all double); src/tickets/tickets.service.spec.ts (add effectiveKeys and replace role/member eligibility assertions); src/projects/members/project-members.service.spec.ts (refuse role.binding.global in last-admin protection cases); src/permissions/remaining-route-declarations.spec.ts; test/integration/memory/outbox-envelope.integration.spec.ts (add effectiveKeys holding project.read to its positional TicketsService harness). Preserve the existing route-level keys and their refusal cases. The all-project integration uses a MEMBER user plus member and custom GLOBAL project.read bindings, no project source, and verifies soft-deleted projects stay excluded.
Workspace home selection is a subtle downstream effect, not a new algorithm: apps/api/src/fleet/threads/workspace-threads.service.ts:43-59 gets reachable projects from ProjectsService, and :76-85 keeps a user display-membership lookup but delegates the agent membership branch to resolveMembership. Therefore globally privileged agents gain home-project reach through US-001/002. Keep the user branch and findMembershipRole; its old roster/global-reach comments must not be mistaken for the new agent gate.

US-003 FINDINGS AND IMPACT
apps/api/src/koda-domain-writer/koda-domain-writer.service.ts:23-32 fixes constructor order; parameter four is AgentAuthProvider today and becomes PermissionService while all others retain positions. :58-70 implements the parallel legacy allow-list that excludes VERIFIER, while :78-94, :126-135 and :163-172 load legacy roles before event transactions. Replace those three paths with assertActorInProject using the exported PROJECT_ACCESS_KEY and the correct USER/AGENT ref. Validate input and project existence first; permission failure happens before opening a transaction, creating an event or recording outbox data. Keep event/outbox atomicity and provenance unchanged. Delete PrismaKodaDomainWriterRepository.findUserProjectRoles (located at apps/api/src/koda-domain-writer/prisma-koda-domain-writer.repository.ts:28). apps/api/src/koda-domain-writer/koda-domain-writer.module.ts:9-12 imports AuthModule only for that old provider and must drop it; rely on the global permissions module. All five stories are security-critical and use three-session-tdd with strict test/implementation isolation. Use PermissionService doubles for claim/binding-disagreement unit cases: a real User.role ADMIN row intentionally still grants legacy admin compatibility through PermissionService. Module/DI wiring regression tests should be colocated unit specs with external collaborators mocked, not new DB-only wiring suites.
